messages:
Maya: Uploading Umbra LoRA merge into staging — attaching a quick eval pack. Need a sanity compatibility check with int4 quant + tokenizer remap. TL;DR: baseline vs merged LoRA, int8/int4, and a small behavioral testset.
Ben: Got it. Can you paste the command you used to build the pack?
Maya: Sure — run locally or CI:```./scripts/gen_evalpack.sh --model umbra/base --lora merges/umbra-lora.safetensors --out /tmp/umbra-pack --quant int4 --token-map remap.json --seed 42```
Li: Running now on a dev GPU, will post results in ~10m. Heads-up: tokenizer remap has a couple of OOV fallbacks, might shift token IDs for customer-specific tokens.
Evan: Important: if token remap shifts frequent customer tokens, generation logits can degrade even without weight regressions. Recommend doing the 50-sample token-level alignment diff first.
Maya: Good call — I included a small script:```python compare_token_alignment.py --base-tokenizer tok.json --remap remap.json --out diffs.csv```
Li: Quick log snippet from the first 200 samples (int4):
```
[2024-06-15 14:02:12] sample=0123: top1 mismatch rate 0.078
[2024-06-15 14:02:12] sample=0456: token-shift detected at pos 3 -> customer_token_42
[2024-06-15 14:02:13] overall ppl delta +0.6 (base->merged,int4)
```
Ben: +0.6 ppl delta is small but not negligible. Do we see any behavioral regressions on generation quality for the customer prompt set?
Li: Ran the quick behavioral eval (50 prompts): 4 prompts showed hallucination/formatting issues vs base. Two of those correlate with token remap events.
QA Bot: Smoke eval summary (umbra-lora, int4): pass criteria: ppl_delta <= +1.0, hall_rate <= 5%. Results -> ppl_delta +0.6, hall_rate 8%, tokenizer_shift_count 14, perf (latency) +12% on small batch. Status: WARNING.
Maya: Hmm — hall_rate 8% > threshold. The 4 problem prompts: I can share diffs. Should we retry with int8 quant or tweak remap?
Evan: Try fallback plan: 1) run int8 quant and compare; 2) run prefix caching enabled to rule out batching latency; 3) quick fix: pin remap for the two problematic customer tokens to original IDs.
Ben: Agree. Also add a tiny A/B rollout policy in staging to route 5% traffic to merged LoRA so we can monitor in prod-like env.
Maya: I'll regenerate pack with int8 and patched remap, then re-run. New command:```./scripts/gen_evalpack.sh --model umbra/base --lora merges/umbra-lora.safetensors --out /tmp/umbra-pack-int8 --quant int8 --token-map remap-patch.json --seed 42```
Li: Running int8 now. ETA 8m.
deploy-bot: CI job #4821 started: run=evalpack-smoke-umbra branch=feature/umbra-lora commit=3f7a9d 
QA Bot: CI result (int8 pack): ppl_delta +0.35, hall_rate 3%, tokenizer_shift_count 2, latency +8%. Status: PASS ✅
Evan: Nice. If int8 passes and int4 fails, we need to document cost/quality tradeoff for customer — some customers prefer determinism over cost.
Maya: Agree. I'll write up a short note and recommend int8 for Umbra unless they accept the small risk. Drafting now and will post to the customer onboarding folder. @Ben @Evan anything else?
Ben: Please include the exact seeds, evalpack version, and the remap diff in the note. Also add a suggested canary config: 5% traffic, 1h monitoring window, auto-rollback on hall_rate > 6%.
Maya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
